parking-yosemite-village.summary: The largest of the three public day-use lots in the Valley and the usual first stop for drivers heading to the shuttle.
parking-yosemite-village.accessibility: Marked accessible spaces. The EV chargers are in the Welcome Center's east lot and are listed as their own place.

parking-yosemite-falls.summary: Public day-use lot serving Yosemite Falls, Camp 4 and the Lodge area.
parking-yosemite-falls.accessibility: Ten Level 2 chargers sit in this lot; see the EV charging entry.

parking-curry-east.summary: Part of the main Curry Village parking, beside the eastbound shuttle stop.
parking-curry-east.accessibility: Twenty Level 2 chargers are spread across the Curry Village lots.

parking-curry-orchard.summary: The orchard section of the main Curry Village parking.

parking-curry-west.summary: Part of the main Curry Village parking, beside the westbound shuttle stop.

parking-bridalveil.summary: Public lot at the start of the Bridalveil Fall paths.

parking-sentinel-bridge.summary: A small public lot between Sentinel Bridge and Cook's Meadow.

parking-el-capitan-meadow.summary: Signed roadside spaces along the meadow.
parking-el-capitan-meadow.notice: Keep off the vegetation and never leave a car where it narrows the road.

parking-trailhead.summary: Overnight parking reserved for people holding a wilderness permit.

parking-welcome-center.summary: A small lot next to the Welcome Center.
parking-welcome-center.notice: It fills quickly; Yosemite Village Parking is the dependable day-use choice.
parking-welcome-center.accessibility: Four Level 2 chargers are close by.

parking-village-store.summary: A small lot intended for Village Store customers.
parking-village-store.notice: It fills quickly; Yosemite Village Parking is the dependable day-use choice.

parking-happy-isles-center.summary: Accessible spaces at the end of the restricted Happy Isles road.
parking-happy-isles-center.accessibility: Only vehicles showing an accessible placard may use these spaces.

parking-happy-isles-restroom.summary: Accessible spaces beside the Happy Isles restroom.
parking-happy-isles-restroom.accessibility: Only vehicles showing an accessible placard may use these spaces.

parking-mirror-lake.summary: Accessible spaces close to the Mirror Lake trailhead.
parking-mirror-lake.accessibility: Only vehicles showing an accessible placard may use these spaces.

parking-exploration-center.summary: Marked accessible spaces at the Exploration Center.
parking-exploration-center.accessibility: Only vehicles showing an accessible placard may use these spaces.

parking-sentinel-beach.summary: A small lot at Sentinel Beach close to the Four Mile Trailhead, with picnic tables, grills, vault toilets and seasonal access to the river.
parking-sentinel-beach.notice: The pin is the NPS picnic-area point rather than a surveyed lot entrance. Read the posted hours before a long Four Mile Trail day; the lot may not be open when you get back.
parking-sentinel-beach.accessibility: Paths are unpaved and mostly level. The 2022 NPS accessibility guide describes uneven parking with no marked accessible spaces, so confirm on arrival.

parking-swinging-bridge.summary: A small lot for the Swinging Bridge picnic area and nearby Valley paths, and a fallback for Four Mile Trail hikers.
parking-swinging-bridge.notice: Space is limited. The pin sits at the centre of the NPS parking polygon, not at a surveyed entrance, and no walking route has been checked.
parking-swinging-bridge.accessibility: Marked accessible spaces, accessible picnic tables and vault toilets. The picnic ground is unpaved but level and paved, mostly flat walkways reach the bridge; the beach itself is not wheelchair accessible.

welcome-center.summary: Ranger information desk, maps, Junior Ranger booklets, lost and found, gifts and passport stamps.
welcome-center.accessibility: Wheelchair accessible, with accessible restrooms and Wi-Fi.

details.label: Road and weather recording
details.text: Dial 209-372-0200, then 1 and 1 again, for the latest recorded road conditions; the recording also covers weather. NPS points out that its web road table only shows planned or long-term closures, so listen to the recording before winter trips and whenever conditions shift.

details.label: Talking to a ranger
details.text: Dial 3, then 5, for general questions between 9 am and 4 pm Pacific (closed over lunch). Those are phone hours; the building's own hours are listed separately.

exploration-center.summary: Changing exhibits, the Spirit of Yosemite film, park books and gifts.
exploration-center.accessibility: Wheelchair accessible; exhibits include tactile and audio elements.

yosemite-museum.summary: Indoor and outdoor exhibits, cultural demonstrations and a museum shop.

wilderness-center.summary: Where wilderness permits are picked up and trips are planned with staff.
wilderness-center.accessibility: Wheelchair accessible. NPS points to marked accessible parking behind the Post Office next door.

ansel-adams-gallery.summary: Fine-art prints, photography, books and gifts, with exhibitions and classes.
ansel-adams-gallery.notice: A visitor reported in September 2026 that batteries and phone chargers were for sale here. Stock changes, so ask the gallery before you count on it.

degnans-kitchen.summary: Coffee, breakfast, deli sandwiches and grab-and-go food, with indoor seating and public Wi-Fi.

village-grill.summary: Burgers, sandwiches, hot dogs and soft serve at outdoor tables.

village-store.summary: The Valley's widest range of groceries, gifts and supplies.

village-bike-rentals.summary: Rental bikes and a tour desk.
village-bike-rentals.notice: Published hours disagree (checked October 25, 2026): Guide 51.8 says 9 am to 5 pm from September 28, while the operator's undated table says 8 am to 7 pm. Both close the 2026 season on October 25, conditions permitting. Ask at the stand for today's hours.

village-post-office.summary: A United States Postal Service branch.
village-post-office.accessibility: Accessible entrance on the west side. NPS points to marked accessible parking west of the Yosemite Museum, linked by paved paths.

yosemite-garage.summary: Vehicle repairs and propane by arrangement. No gasoline is sold anywhere in the Valley.
yosemite-garage.notice: NPS says the garage takes no walk-ins: call 209-372-1060 to arrange repairs or propane. Roadside help and towing run around the clock, and the air hose in front works 24 hours. Confirm before you drive over.
yosemite-garage.accessibility: NPS lists wheelchair access and marked accessible parking at the front (page dated September 26, 2025; checked October 26, 2026).

details.label: Getting through
details.text: The roadside number is the direct line for towing and breakdowns. Visitors have suggested the Yosemite Hospitality (Aramark) switchboard as another way to reach the garage and other concession services; its hours and whether it transfers calls have not been checked.

medical-clinic.summary: Urgent and primary care. This is not an emergency room: call or text 911 for emergencies.
medical-clinic.notice: NPS clinic page dated September 2 (checked October 23, 2026): urgent-care hours depend on staffing, few insurance plans are accepted and out-of-state patients should expect to pay directly. Phone first.

mariposa-library.summary: A county library branch with public computers and Wi-Fi.
mariposa-library.notice: Hours follow the county schedule; check it once you have signal.

ahwahnee-hotel.summary: The historic hotel, with dining rooms, shops and guest services.

ahwahnee-dining-room.summary: Fine dining; book ahead for dinner.

details.label: Reservations
details.text: Guide 51.8 strongly recommends dinner reservations by phone (209-372-1489) or on OpenTable. The operator's page, checked October 5, 2026, adds that a hotel booking does not guarantee a table and steers guests to OpenTable.

details.label: Dress
details.text: Guide 51.8 calls for appropriate attire at dinner. The operator spells it out: long trousers with a collared shirt, or a dress, skirt or trousers with a blouse; no hiking clothes, shorts, T-shirts, tank tops, flip-flops or baseball caps. Breakfast and brunch are casual.

details.label: Afternoon tea
details.text: Served 4 to 5 pm daily for hotel guests only, according to the operator.

ahwahnee-bar.summary: Cocktails, wine, appetizers and lighter plates.

details.label: Dress
details.text: Casual clothing is fine at the bar, per the operator's page checked October 5, 2026.

ahwahnee-sweet-shop.summary: Coffee, sweets, snacks and a few provisions.

curry-village.summary: A lodging hub with restaurants, a store, rentals, public showers and parking.
curry-village.notice: The operator's lodging page (checked October 23, 2026) says Curry Village closes November 29 to December 10, 2026. Confirm which guest services are affected; nearby activities may still run.

curry-bar-1899.summary: Craft beer, cocktails and light meals, inside or out.

curry-seven-tents.summary: Home-style breakfast and dinner with indoor seating.

curry-pizza-deck.summary: Pizza by the pie or slice, salads and garlic bread on an outdoor deck.

curry-meadow-grill.summary: Counter-service tacos and burritos with outdoor seating.
curry-meadow-grill.notice: Seasonal; it reopens in spring or summer. Check once you have signal.

mountain-shop.summary: Hiking and climbing gear and clothing.

mountaineering-school.summary: Guided hikes, climbing instruction and other outdoor programs.
mountaineering-school.notice: Operator guidance checked October 25, 2026: lessons and guided climbs must be reserved, while gear rentals are first-come with no reservations. Confirm before travelling.

curry-bike-rentals.summary: Rental bikes and a tour desk.
curry-bike-rentals.notice: Published hours disagree (checked October 25, 2026): Guide 51.8 says 9 am to 5 pm from September 28, while the operator's undated table says 8 am to 7 pm. Both close the 2026 season on October 25, conditions permitting. Ask at the stand for today's hours.

curry-raft-rentals.summary: Raft rentals on the Merced when the river allows it.
curry-raft-rentals.notice: Seasonal and dependent on river conditions, usually late spring into summer.

curry-pool.summary: A seasonal pool, open when conditions allow.

curry-ice-rink.summary: An outdoor rink with skating sessions of two and a half hours, conditions permitting.
curry-ice-rink.notice: Seasonal; the opening date depends on conditions.

valley-lodge.summary: A lodging hub with restaurants, a gift shop, tour desk, bike rentals and a pool.

base-camp-eatery.summary: Counter service for breakfast, burgers, chicken, pasta and more.

lodge-starbucks.summary: Coffee, snacks and a light breakfast.

lodge-gift-shop.notice: Guide 51.8 prints 8 am to 9 pm; the operator's undated lodge page says 8 am to 8 pm. Check the closing time at the door.

lodge-bike-rentals.summary: Adaptive bikes must be reserved in advance; call the Lodge stand to book an ADA scooter. Wheelchair rentals are listed without a reservation policy. Standard bikes are first-come, so confirm availability.
lodge-bike-rentals.notice: Published hours disagree (checked October 25, 2026): Guide 51.8 says 9 am to 5 pm from September 28, while the operator's undated table says 8 am to 7 pm. Both close the 2026 season on October 25, conditions permitting. Ask at the stand for today's hours.

housekeeping-camp.summary: Seasonal riverside lodging in numbered units with concrete walls, a canvas roof, patio, bear locker and fire ring. The operator counts 266 units; the NPS building labels used for pins are not a booking inventory.
housekeeping-camp.notice: Search Places for a unit number, for example 'Housekeeping site 179'. Unit pins are approximate building centres; the front desk confirms where your unit is.

details.label: The unit
details.text: Three concrete walls, a canvas roof, a privacy curtain and a covered patio. A standard unit sleeps up to six with a double bed, twin bunks and two optional cots. There are lights and outlets but no phone or TV.

details.label: Arriving
details.text: Check-in is at 4 pm and check-out at 11 am. Bring bedding or rent it on site. The desk is staffed around the clock during the season.

details.label: Services and access
details.text: Non-guests may use the laundry for a fee. The showers are only for registered guests; Curry Village sells public showers. Shuttle stop 12 is the camp's stop.

details.label: Food and fire
details.text: Everything with a scent, including coolers, toiletries and rubbish, goes in a closed, latched bear locker. Every unit has a grill and fire ring; wood fires are allowed only 5 to 10 pm and any current restrictions apply.

details.label: House rules
details.text: Quiet hours run 10 pm to 6 am. No pets other than service animals. Sleeping in vehicles or outside the units is not allowed.

details.label: Accessible units
details.text: Ask for an accessible unit when booking. The operator describes nearby parking, paved paths and accessible toilets, but the accessibility of any particular numbered unit has not been checked.

housekeeping-store.summary: Basic supplies and camping items in the office building, which also handles registration. Firewood and rental bedding come through camp staff.
housekeeping-store.accessibility: NPS lists the store as accessible; ask staff about the best approach.

housekeeping-laundry.summary: Coin washers and dryers near the registration office and showers. NPS says non-guests are welcome to use it.
housekeeping-laundry.accessibility: NPS lists the laundry as accessible; ask staff about the best approach.

housekeeping-showers.summary: Shower houses next to registration and the laundry, with soap and towels, for registered Housekeeping guests only. Curry Village has paid public showers.
housekeeping-showers.accessibility: NPS lists accessible showers. The pin marks the men's shower building; ask staff for the accessible entrance.

conservation-heritage-center.summary: Seasonal exhibits, a natural-history library and information.
conservation-heritage-center.accessibility: The historic stone steps rule out wheelchair access.

happy-isles-center.summary: Exhibits, drop-in activities and seasonal art classes.
happy-isles-center.accessibility: The building is accessible; driving in and parking require an accessible placard.

yosemite-chapel.summary: A historic chapel with community services.

upper-pines-campground.summary: Reservation campground near Happy Isles and the East Valley shuttle.

lower-pines-campground.summary: Reservation campground on the bank of the Merced.

north-pines-campground.summary: Reservation campground between the Merced and Tenaya Creek.

camp-4.summary: A walk-in campground with a long place in climbing history.
camp-4.notice: Booking rules change by season; check Recreation.gov.
